newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut hotel company SGHL to list shares.
newsitem.headline: Beirut hotel company SGHL to list shares.

text.p: The shareholders of Societe des Grands Hotels du Liban (SGHL), which is restoring two major Beirut hotels, approved a capital increase for the company, Lebanon Invest finance house said on Thursday.
The company plans to list its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange soon.

Shareholders approved a debt and equity package completed in September at two recent meetings and also appointed a new board including foreign subscribers to the capital increase, Omar Jaroudi of Lebanon Invest told Reuters.
The package for restoration of the two hotels comprises a capital increase from 528 million Lebanese pounds to 160 billion pounds ($103 million) and loans totalling $55 million.
Shareholders approved the capital increase -- a 104 billion pounds asset revaluation and a $35 million equity increase by private placement and cash injection -- on October 17 and 21, Jaroudi said.

SGHL is undertaking the restoration of the 572-room Phoenicia Intercontinental and the 96-room Vendome Intercontinental which were gutted during the 1975-90 civil war. Work on the Vendome is almost complete.
Under the asset revaluation shareholders receive 197 shares for each old one and those contributing fully to the capital increase receive 105 shares for each old one, Jaroudi said.

"The next step is to issue nominative share certificates until bearer shares are printed, and then we can go on the Beirut Stock Exchange," Jaroudi told Reuters after two shareholders meetings which approved the operations.
"We have pre-authorisation to list and expect to do so in two or three months," he said.
Lebanon Invest was carrying out research in preparation for issuing a recommendation on SGHL shares, which will be the first of a hotel company to be listed on the Beirut market, Jaroudi said.
The new shareholders are from Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Lebanon, Kuwait, the Gulf Emirates, Switzerland, Britain, and the Intercontinental Hotels and Resort Co., Jaroudi said.

The new 12-member board includes five major subscribers in the equity increase. Chairman Mazen Salha and his brother Marwan retain their posts and the board includes five other individuals and representatives of five institutions -- three Lebanese, one U.K. and one from the Gulf, Jaroudi said.
Refurbishment of the Vendome, near the Beirut seafront beside the pre-war grand hotels district, is almost complete and it will have a soft opening on November 1.

Tender documents from construction companies bidding to restore the Phoenicia -- one of the pre-war grand hotels -- were expected in November and work should start before the end of the year, he added.
Twelve companies pre-qualified and seven were expected to bid, Jaroudi said.
